0620-0655: Val and I birded the Garden Inn grounds waiting for Fran. The weather was pre-sun and post-rain, partly cloudy and mild, with calm winds. (Low-light conditions hampered photography). 

0716-1300: Southern Glades Management Area, Aerojet Road north and south of State Road 9336 -- an epic visit to see what was around. We walked south to just beyond the land bridge beyond the yellow gate to about 0.3 miles north of State Road 9336, then returned to the parking area. We did not walk around "Lucky Hammock" owing to the tall, soaked vegetation. We spent some time at the parking area chatting with Bryant Roberts, whom I had not seen in at least 15 years. Larry Manfredi joined us at 1135 to help us find a White-tailed Kite (a lifer for Fran), which we would not have found without him -- I didn't realize that you had to walk so far north of State Road 9336 to find a kite. The weather was partly sunny and cool, with calm winds at the start, ending with overcast skies and fairly heavy rain for the final 12 minutes; we were all rather drenched by the time we arrived back at our cars.

1322-1350: Larry Manfredi's yard, Homestead -- a successful chase of the two Rufous Hummingbirds in Larry's yard, and  a chance to see after many years (Bill) or to meet (Val and Fran) Larry's wife, Christine. The weather was overcast, mild, and humid, with calm winds. We treated Larry to lunch at the Royal Palm Grill 2

1512-1533: Royal Palm Grill 2  parking lot -- chatting with Larry after a delicious meal with a gracious host. The weather was overcast, mild, and humid, with a light breeze. We headed for home afterward.

description:
Small, short-tailed hummingbird with classic COHU features such as purple gorget, white eyebrow, short tail, wingtips extending beyond tip of tail, etc. However, there are a couple odd features about this bird. For one, the bill was straighter than I expected. The other was its call; as it responded to an Anna's across the garden, it made a call quite similar to an ANHU display call. Admittedly I haven't heard a lot of COHU to appreciate all the sounds they can make, but for what its worth the call is very different from anything I've heard from a COHU. I may be off base here, but I'm going to suggest that we at least consider the possibility of a hybrid.
 
 Attached are some photos and my audio clip for others with more experience to consider.

El individuo se posó brevemente en una pequeña rama antes de volver a desplazarse entre la vegetación.

description:
Este individuo lleva desde inicios de julio de 2025 hasta estos momentos (enero de 2026) donde llega a un arbusto espinoso en la ventana de mi cuarto para dormir. Llega a las 6:40 PM y se retira a las 6:40 AM (aproximadamente) no tiene un horario exacto entre las 6:43 am para levantarse o 6:50 pm para acostarse dónde antes de acostarse suele mostrar un comportamiento un poco alterado donde vuela y se posa repetidamente en la rama del arbusto y moviendo mucho la cola cuando esta posado hasta que se queda en estado de topor.

This individual has been returning to the same thorny bush outside my bedroom window to sleep since early July 2025 (continuing through January 2026). Its routine is very consistent, arriving around 6:40 PM and departing around 6:40 AM, with slight variations between 6:50 PM for settling in and 6:43 AM for waking up. Before roosting, it displays a somewhat restless behavior, repeatedly flying and perching on the branches while constantly flicking its tail. It continues this until it finally enters a state of torpor for the night.

A couple of the hummingbirds landed and perched long enough for visual examination through 10x binoculars and even a photo. One of the perched birds showed a small orange patch on a whitish / buff throat with brown streaks, a long bill, reddish pink flanks, and a dull olive - green back and top of head. Another bird, distinctly larger, looked very similar but without the orange throat patch and more pronounced rusty flanks and whitish tips on the tail when the bird flew away. The plumage patterns match that of the rufous hummingbird, probably an adult female and an immature male. The other hummingbirds are judged to also be rufous hummingbirds but of unknown age and sex.

With Valeri Ponzo and Steve Backes; a successful chase of the Black-chinned Hummingbird (a Florida lifer for Val and a photographic lifer for me), along with the Rufous Hummingbird; this was the first three-hummingbird-day-in-Florida for either of us.. The weather was overcast, chilly/cool (64 degrees but the humidity made it seem much chillier), and humid, with a light breeze. As always, Steve was a great and gracious host. We arrived at 1530 and left at 1731.

With Valeri Ponzo; a full day of local birding. I drove to Sarasota in the morning and met Val at her Center Road home.

I include only those spots where I took photographs. Our itinerary for today was:

0816: Center Road, Val's former home -- I took a couple photographs as we were leaving.

0833-1116: Twin Lakes Park -- a successful chase of the Rufous Hummingbird, a Sarasota County bird for each of us. The weather was sunny and cool with a light breeze at the start, becoming hot (87 degrees, "feels like" 91) and breezy by the end. We stayed at the (planted) Powderpuff Mimosa until we both got great looks at the hummingbird (less than 30 minutes), then walked around the western lake clockwise then around the eastern lake clockwise south all the way to the retention pond, then east along Hawkins Road around the ballfields (which were all active with baseball or soccer games), then finally through the playground and eventually back to Jet. We left at 1116 and headed to Gecko's for lunch.

1240-1255: Gecko's Restaurant -- we birded the grounds before eating lunch. The weather was sunny, warm, and breezy.

1348-1433: Manatee County Landfill -- Apparently because I failed to stop at the check station, a bulldozer operator acted like he was going to ram us, and then was a total ahole the rest of our visit (chasing away the gulls while we were scanning them). It was not a fun visit, and neither of us has been back. The weather was sunny, hottish, and breezy. 

1455-1618: Nathan Benderson Park, Sarasota -- With nobody trying to harm us, we spent some time here, examining the gull flock (there were more than 350 American Herring Gulls here) and the shorebirds roosting on the gated-off sections of the park through the lake.

1618-1815: Mote Science Education Aquarium, under construction. The site was surprisingly birdy, with birds using the lakes and temporary wetlands -- we walked past the south side of the site along North Cattlemen Road.

After taking Val home, I drove back to Spring Hill, arriving at 2018.
